subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should restart-safe plugin storage become available to third-party plugins, and should agent-local storage extend the existing keyed-store API or remain limited to trusted first-party runtime surfaces?
rationale: The choice establishes a new persisted plugin SDK contract, cross-agent isolation model, resource-abuse boundary, and database lifecycle that cannot be inferred safely from the proposed table alone.

options.title: Extend the keyed store
options.body: Add an explicit agent-bound keyed-store variant while preserving the existing plugin-global store and enforcing trust, quotas, lifecycle, and isolation contracts.

options.title: Keep storage plugin-global
options.body: Retain the current store and require plugins to encode agent identity in supported namespaces only where maintainers accept the shared-database lifecycle.

options.title: Keep third-party state plugin-owned
options.body: Do not expose host-managed agent storage and require external plugins to maintain their own SQLite databases through the existing plugin-state helpers.

recommendation.title: Extend the keyed store
recommendation.body: Add an explicit agent-bound keyed-store variant while preserving the existing plugin-global store and enforcing trust, quotas, lifecycle, and isolation contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects this contributor most closely to plugin SDK boundaries, keyed-state behavior, and official-plugin trust handling.
